name: Bonebind Orator
description: {3}{B}, Exile this card from your graveyard: Return target creature card other than this one from your graveyard to your hand.
assumptions: Read node C (move, gy→exile, thing:self, flags 'cost:{3}{B}') as the activation cost itself — exiling this card from the graveyard, paid alongside {3}{B} — rather than as a separate effect, since C's `to` is 'exile' (not 'stack') and C→D is therefore an automatic, non-interruptible continuation: paying the cost (C) leads straight into the effect (D) with nothing else able to happen in between.
Treated the A→B (cast→enters) chain as ordinary card mechanics — casting this creature and it entering the battlefield — rather than a printed ability, since B has no further steps hanging off it.

Worded D's 'target not:self' as 'target creature card other than this one,' reading 'creature' per the schema's coarse-type-word convention (a creature CARD, matching D's from:gy/to:hand zones, not a creature permanent).
couldNotDerive: Whether activating the graveyard ability is restricted to sorcery speed (or any other timing restriction) — the schema's flag vocabulary has no field for activation timing, so nothing in the nodes speaks to this either way.
Rarity and any supertype (withheld/undetermined by the packet).
notes:
Confirmed via forge-model/data/bonebind-orator.txt: Name Bonebind Orator, ManaCost {1}{B}, Types Creature Squirrel Warlock Bard, PT 2/2, Oracle '{3}{B}, Exile Bonebind Orator from your graveyard: Return another target creature card from your graveyard to your hand.' Mana cost, type line, and full rules text all match the reconstruction exactly, including the compound cost structure (mana + self-exile as one activation cost) and the effect (return another target creature card from graveyard to hand).

This is a clean fix over attempt 1's two findings. Attempt 1's node C was a bare move (gy→hand, thing:creature, flags 'target not:self') with no cost of any kind and no companion node for the self-exile — the packet was missing the entire '{3}{B}, Exile Bonebind Orator from your graveyard' cost, both the mana portion and the additional-cost portion, and flagged both as could-not-derive rather than wrong (an honest gap, not an invented answer). This regenerated packet now carries exactly the companion node attempt 1's notes predicted was missing: C is now its own move node (gy→exile, thing:self, flags 'cost:{3}{B}'), i.e. 'exile this card from your graveyard' bundled with the {3}{B} mana cost as one activation cost, chained via steps into D (the original gy→hand return, unchanged). That C→D wiring (non-stack, so guaranteed once the cost is paid) is exactly the right shape for an activated ability whose printed effect follows its cost with no intervening priority. The translator fix for the `Cost$ 3 B ExileFromGrave<1/CARDNAME>` compound-cost string (mana + self-exile-from-graveyard sub-cost) is verified working on this card. Attempt 1's secondary schema-expressiveness question — whether SCHEMA.md needs a distinct field for an ability's ActivationZone$ when it differs from the card's default zone — turns out not to be needed here: node C's own `from: gy` already establishes that the cost (and therefore the ability) is paid/activated out of the graveyard, so no additional field was required to convey that fact. No further gaps found; verdict is a full match.
